item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION — Sat Aug 22, 1:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Golden Hour DJ Series at Poynsaurus Brewing Co. — Sat Aug 22, 7:00 PM — Ponysaurus Brewing Co.
item.description:
Our favorite DJs at The Floor and DanceGruv Radio are back in the beer garden for Golden Hour ✨🌅 Grab a High Horse mocktail and float away to electric beats curated by the best DJs in the 919 🕺🪩 See you at sunset, no tickets required!
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Aug 22, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: The Mountain Goats — Sat Aug 22, 8:00 PM — DPAC Presented by First Horizon
item.description: Hi it’s John Darnielle and this is the new Mountain Goats bio. Every time you make a record you have to have a new bio and it’s a whole thing. Sometimes you have to have conversations about who’d be a good person to write the bio and other times one of the press people does it and you vet it and it goes through a whole process, but we are eliminating the middle man this time. My other job involves writing prose and I’m regarded as decent enough at it so let’s fast foward through the prelims here. Days is the something-somethingth album by the Mountain Goats. If that last phrase has a number in it then you will know it has been edited by bad people and you should stop reading now. If it says “something somethingth” then we are still together. Like at least two other tMG albums, specifically Goths and Beat the Champ, Days gets born one day when I have a funny idea. The idea in this case was writing a followup to Goths about the 90s and calling it Grunges. I made this joke on the popular

item.title: Fourth Sunday Social Rides — Sun Aug 23, 10:00 AM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Pull up and ride with us! Black Spoke Society’s Fourth Sunday rides are no-drop, social-paced group rides built for connection, joy, and getting outside together. Whether you’re brand new to cycling, dusting off your bike, or ride every week, you belong here. We roll at a conversational pace, pause when needed, and make sure no one gets left behind. This is about community over competition. Come as you are. Bring a friend. Bring your whole self. Expect: – A chill, steady pace – Good music and even better vibes – Route support and ride leaders – Water + snack stops when needed – Post-ride hangs when the mood is right Helmet required. Lights encouraged. Good energy mandatory. Let’s ride. 🖤🚴🏾‍♀️
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Strength Training Class — Sun Aug 23, 10:30 AM — The Glass Jug Downtown
item.description:
Celebrate the summer season with a fun and challenging Strength workout class with Beltane Strength & Fitness. Highlight your strength, empowerment, and fun with an energizing in-person session just for awesome women like you. Whether you’re a fitness newbie or a workout pro, this event is all about moving, sweating, and supporting each other. Weather permitting, we’ll host the class outside, so dress accordingly! Bring your energy and come thirsty because each ticket includes one draft beer, wine, cider, or THC beverage. View on Facebook.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Beginner Fused and Stained Glass Votives — Sun Aug 23, 2:00 PM — Fusion Gallery
item.description:
Learn the basics of Fused and Stained glass in this combination class series. In day one, students will create 4 small 2X4 inch fused glass panels. In day two, students will learn the tiffany method of copper foiling to solder the panels together to create a custom fused glass votive holder. Students will leave with a finished project after the second session of this class. All materials are included in class pricing. No prior glass experience necessary. Please wear closed-toe shoes and bring something with sleeves.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Drawn From™: Pinterest — A Hand-building Pop-Up at Redhead Hemp — Sun Aug 23, 2:00 PM — Redhead Hemp
item.description:
EarthenTide Studios presents: Drawn From™ is our accessible approach to creating the objects we love from the worlds of design, fashion, and art. We place a purchased object beside an EarthenTide recreation — no labels, no hints — and invite guests to decode the difference. After a short demo and meditation, participants are coached through creating their own unique piece.

item.title: Sunday DRIFT Rooftop DJ Sets at The Velvet Hippo! — Sun Aug 23, 4:00 PM — The Velvet Hippo
item.description:
Every Sunday from 4-7pm, you’ll hear music drifting from the rooftop on Orange Street! Our Sunday afternoon DJ sets are a great way to end your weekend on a high note. Get your crew together to spill the tea while you sip on spritz and mimosa specials and watch the sun get low over the Bull City skyline. This series rotates through your favorite Velvet Hippo DJs, and once a month, the Sunday DRIFT will be a Recovery Tea Dance Edition with Gay Agenda and Father Disco! No cover, 21+ to enter.

item.title: Storytime on the Roof with Durham County Library — Mon Aug 24, 10:30 AM — The Durham Hotel
item.description:

item.title: Durham Chess Club — Wed Aug 26, 5:45 PM — Durham Food Hall
item.description:

item.title: Mobile Health Assessment — Thu Aug 27, 9:30 AM — None
item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Additionally, there is a goal setting and referral session with a nurse, dietitian, or fitness specialist. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.
Source: Duke University

Drop in for an enhanced mindfulness experience through a focus on mobilization.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Duke Farmers Market — Thu Aug 27, 11:00 AM — None
item.description:
Join us for the Duke Farmers Market! Here you can:
Find farm fresh fruits, vegetables, and other local goods at a convenient location. Enjoy a relaxed atmosphere while learning about local food systems and how eating sustainably can positively impact your health. Support local farmers and independently-owned businesses, including community partners like Duke Campus Farm.
The Duke Farmers Market is an annual market sponsored by LIVE FOR LIFE. LIVE FOR LIFE, Duke's employee wellness program, offers a variety of programs and services, such as health assessments, smoking cessation programs, fitness activities, and health education to help eligible faculty, staff and family members reach health and fitness goals.

item.description:

COSMOS - Genie McPeek Hinz: What COSMOS is and how Duke researchers are using it. FCAP - Tracey Hughes: What FCAP is and how Duke researchers are using it. PCORnet, CRDM, and DEDUCE - Nelda Bradley: What these resources are and how they differ. Open Discussion/Q&A Whether you're launching a new study or just want to know what tools are out there, this is a great chance to get oriented and ask questions.

item.title: Critical Thinking: Strategies for Improving — Thu Aug 27, 1:00 PM — None
item.description:

item.title: Organ Demonstration — Thu Aug 27, 1:00 PM — Duke Chapel
item.description:
This organ demonstration is an opportunity to stop in to hear a Duke Chapel organ or Bösendorfer grand piano played in the informal atmosphere of an open rehearsal.
These demonstrations are typically held on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 1:00 to 1:45 p.m. during the academic year. To confirm that a rehearsal is happening on a given day, please email dukechapel@duke.edu.
There is no charge for admission. Paid parking is available on a first-come-first-served basis in the Bryan Center Garage at 125 Science Drive. ADA parking is available in the surface lot at the same address.

item.title: Tree Walk with a Naturalist — Thu Sep 3, 10:00 AM — Prairie Ridge
item.description:

item.title: Luminary & Freedom Stories — Fri Sep 18, 7:00 PM — Bennett Place State Historic Site
item.description:
During this special luminary program, Bennett Place invites you to reflect on the end of the Civil War as a momentous step towards freedom for all Americans and the end of chattel slavery in the United States.
Walk among 3,310 luminaries - one for every 1,000 enslaved people in North Carolina - and reflect on experiences of enslavement and freedom. Historians dot the path and share stories of people's pathways to freedom and life after slavery & the Civil War.
---
Harriet Ann Daves recalled just how monumental Civil War surrenders were for her family: "When the surrender came my grandfather came to my mother and told her: 'Well, you are as free as I am.'"
Claiming freedom was not so straightforward for the 331,059 enslaved women, children, and men in North Carolina during the Civil War. Some took enormous risk to reach Union lines before the federal government made any promise of abolishing slavery. Others left their homes and plantations to follow Sherman's army as they marched

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Nov 20 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place.
